title: Forced P = 2 accuracy budgets of the multi-rank ND KCP rows (declared 2026-11-09T07:57:07Z)
rule: budget = max(the G1 cell of the same (row, CP, tensor) in cake_gdn_det_train_kcp_g1_budgets.json, 1.10 x max over sm_100a / sm_103a / sm_107a of the deterministic package's measured error at the forced P = 2), rel-RMS and max-abs each; the measured error is the max over the forced forms the ND dist test runs on the row (segments=2, NaN-filled allocations: save_transfer=False with save_mode light and full; with use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel also save_transfer on, for out / dv / dg / dbeta, since the l2n rows judge dq / dk against FP64 by rel-RMS alone), against the FP64 reference of the global unpadded pack (out / dq / dk / dv as stored BF16, dg / dbeta as FP32)
max_abs_slack: max-abs may exceed budget_max_abs by one storage ulp of |ref| at the candidate's worst element (judge_tensor pass_u1); rel-RMS has no slack
applies_to: the comparisons of tests/experimental/test_cake_gdn_nondet_train_kcp_dist.py made with forced=True: the arms at the forced P = 2 of the rows whose ranks all plan P = 1 (_p2_full_arms, the l2n rows' forced light_akk forms, the poison pairs' forced forms), against FP64 and against their partner arm; every other comparison keeps the G1 cell

measured_at.harness: the dist test's rows, operands, partition, FP64 references, NaN-filled allocations and judge, imported as a library

sm_100a.launch: 8 ranks x 1 node (8 GPUs per node)

sm_103a.launch: 8 ranks x 2 nodes (4 GPUs per node)

sm_107a.launch: 8 ranks x 2 nodes (4 GPUs per node)

no_forced_form.A4: plans P > 1 on some rank at CP 8 (sm_100a P = [24]; sm_103a P = [25]; sm_107a P = [35]): the test runs no forced form

notes: a multi-rank row whose CP has no cell here is judged at the row's nearest CP of record, as in the G1 table (A1-cp16 -> the A1 CP8 cell; not measured at CP16)
det_p2 / nd_p2 per tensor: [rel-RMS, max-abs] per architecture, max over the forced forms of the rule
measurements: the deterministic package's error per forced form and architecture; bitwise: whether ND and det agree bit for bit per form (all six tensors)
